tool_input.description: Find tests for the swallowed-jq checker

tool_input.command:
grep -n "jq empty\|refusing to write\|echo \"\$content\"\|GUARD (bug" head/.claude/scripts/ledger-lib.sh
echo ---
grep -n "except OSError\|except ValueError\|except FileNotFoundError\|_SemaphoreExhausted" head/.claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/agy_headless_adapter.py
echo ---
grep -n "in_heredoc\|_start_heredoc\|hd_exec\|Step 1\|Step 3" head/tools/check-no-swallowed-jq.sh
tool_input.description: Get exact line numbers for citations in head files

result:
Review written to `review.md`. Summary: **CHANGES_REQUIRED** — two of the three "simplifications" actually remove targeted safety protections rather than just trimming code:

1. **`ledger-lib.sh`** — the content guard was weakened from "valid JSON object, exactly one value" to just "parses as JSON," reopening a narrower version of the exact ledger-truncation bug (20260808-a008c6) the guard's own comment cites (e.g. literal `null` or concatenated multi-doc JSON now slip through).
2. **`agy_headless_adapter.py`** — removing the `ValueError` handler means an embedded-NUL-byte argv failure now propagates uncaught instead of converting to `ProviderUnavailableError`, breaking the documented multi-model chain-walk fallback guarantee.
3. **`check-no-swallowed-jq.sh`** — heredoc bodies piped to an interpreter are now unconditionally skipped, losing real detection coverage for the exact "swallowed jq" shape the tool exists to catch (not just reducing false positives on test fixtures, as the comment implies).

All findings include exact `head/` file:line citations and suggested minimal fixes that preserve the intended simplification without the regression.
